morphology.motility: Non-motile — lacks flagella (twitching motility via pili in some strains)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil and water; also colonizes human skin
habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental organism and opportunistic nosocomial pathogen; notably resilient on hospital surfaces
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Survives desiccation for extended periods, contributing to persistence on hospital equipment/surfaces

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative coccobacilli, can resist decolorization and appear Gram-variable

culture.growthCharacteristics: Strict aerobe, grows readily on routine media

identificationClues: Gram-negative coccobacillus, oxidase NEGATIVE — distinguishes it from Pseudomonas and Neisseria
Notorious for extensive multidrug resistance in healthcare settings
Survives well on dry hospital surfaces, contributing to outbreaks

virulenceFactors: Extensive intrinsic and acquired antibiotic resistance mechanisms
clinicalImportance.transmission: Nosocomial — contaminated surfaces, ventilator equipment, healthcare worker hands; notable in ICU and burn-unit outbreaks and in combat-related wound infections
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Recognized by the CDC and WHO as a critical-priority multidrug-resistant (including carbapenem-resistant) pathogen due to limited treatment options
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Oxidase-negative distinguishes it from Pseudomonas aeruginosa, another common non-fermenting Gram-negative nosocomial pathogen it can otherwise resemble clinically

examFacts.importantTest: Oxidase test (negative) to distinguish from Pseudomonas
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Oxidase negative and highly resistant to desiccation, unlike Pseudomonas aeruginosa
